key_insight: Aggregate scores can hide weaknesses in next-visit diagnosis prediction; LONGINUS combines retrieval and memory to better predict persistent, newly recorded, and recurrent diagnoses.
clinical_relevance: Transition-specific evaluation helps distinguish prediction of future documented diagnoses from simple repetition of prior records, without establishing clinical benefit.
method: Evaluate diagnosis predictions by set size, label frequency, temporal transition, and observed history depth.
Combine retrieved patient-record evidence with structured memory of the patient trajectory.
Preserve predictions shared across views and adjudicate disagreements without revealing their source.
evidence_signal: Across MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV with four LLM backbones, LONGINUS led LLM-based methods on transition-specific performance in nearly all settings, while repeating the last visit outperformed most LLM approaches overall.
watch_item: The abstract reports retrospective prediction of documented diagnoses, not prospective clinical benefit; cross-view agreement is a reliability heuristic rather than proof of correctness.
paper_title: Rethinking Next-Visit Diagnosis Prediction Beyond Aggregate Metrics: Retrieval--Memory Multi-Agent Adjudication
